To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nit2, nit3 and nit1 genes are arranged in a gene cluster, that the genes have a similar architecture, that they have a similar expression pattern and that they encode nitrilases that are active at the pH of the apoplastic space.
the Arabidopsis nitrilase genes are organized in a cluster and that their expression is tissue-specific.

the nit2/nir1/nit3 cluster encodes three nitrilases that catalyze the terminal step of indole-acetic-acid biosynthesis in Arabisopsis thaliana, that the genes show high sequence identity, that the promoters of nit2 and nit3 are very different from that of nit1 and that nit1 expression is highest in fully expanded leaflets and in the apices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the nit2, nitl and nit3 nitrilase genes of Arabidopsis thalanica.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of auxin biosynthetic processes in plants.
the identification and molecular characterization of genes encoding enzymes involved in auxin biosynthesis, and with their regulation by the developmental program and environmental factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nitrilases are involved in IAA biosynthesis in Arabdopsis thaliana.
the three isoforms of nitrilase are expressed in a highly coordinated manner, but in a spatially and temporally restricted manner.

auxin biosynthesis is a highly regulated process, which may be subject to fine tuning by a variety of developmental and environmental cues, and that nitrilases are likely to play a key role as a rate-limiting step in the biosynthesis of auxin in Arabidopsis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three Arabidopsis nitrilases are encoded by a single gene cluster and that the genes are expressed in a tissue-specific manner.
the nit2/n1/n3 gene cluster encodes three nitrilases with different expression patterns, which are likely to be involved in the biosynthesis of IAA in Arabidopsis.
nit3 expression is restricted to the root apex and to the shoot apex, whereas nit1 and nit2 expression is found in both apical regions and in the shoot and root system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nit1 gene is expressed in a manner that is consistent with a role in indole-acetamide biosynthesis, whereas nit2 and nit3 are expressed at much lower levels and are likely to be involved in the biosynthesis of other nitriles.
auxin biosynthesis is not restricted to the root tip and that auxin biosynthetic genes are not only expressed there.

the nitrilases encoded by the nit2/nitr1/nitr3 gene cluster in Arabidopsis are likely to have a role in auxin biosynthesis, but their expression patterns suggest that their contribution to auxin biosynthesis in different tissues of the plant might be very different.
